claims.text: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has severe lattice distortions arising from its random elemental distribution.
Heating equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr to 700–900°C partially relaxes its local lattice distortions.
Relaxation of lattice distortion modifies dislocation-core configurations.
The dislocation-core changes favor edge-dislocation motion.
Rapid quenching from high temperature can produce a single-phase BCC state in equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
The proposed controlled comparison uses RT, 500°C, 700°C, and 900°C tests at approximately 1×10^-4 s^-1.
The single-phase BCC structure of HfNbTaTiZr remains stable through 900°C.
Thermal activation becomes significant in the 700–900°C range.
Local atomic rearrangements at elevated temperature partially relieve lattice distortion.
Relief of lattice distortion lowers the energy barriers for edge-dislocation motion.
Between 700°C and 900°C, yield strength decreases relative to RT and 500°C.
Between 700°C and 900°C, the thermal-expansion coefficient increases nonlinearly and more rapidly than at lower temperatures.
Elastic anisotropy increases modestly at elevated temperature.
Elevated-temperature microstructures show a shift toward edge-dislocation dominance or enhanced edge mobility.
At RT and through 500°C, the lattice remains strongly distorted and undergoes minimal thermal relaxation.
The proposed effects are limited to single-phase BCC HfNbTaTiZr from RT to 900°C with minimal secondary phases.

contradictions.description: The initial BCC state is described as metastable, whereas the conditions and boundary describe the BCC phase as stable through 900°C without distinguishing kinetic retention from thermodynamic stability.
